transcript: [02:05] Man: Hello?
[02:06] Woman: Hi, good morning, this is Talia from Parrot Bay Travel Agency. Is Robert Goddard there?
[02:11] Man: Yes, speaking.
[02:13] Woman: I’m so sorry that I made such an early phone call, and i’m calling to ask a few questions about your most recent vacation - could i have five minutes of your time?
[02:22] Man: Sure thing.
[02:23] Woman: Great, thanks. Now, I see here that you visited Melbourne. Was this your first visit to Melbourne?
[02:29] Man: No, I have actually been there twice before.
[02:32] Woman: I see. Now, what would you say was your favorite part about Melbourne?
[02:36] Man: Well, I did like seeing the exotic wildlife, and there are great sites to see, but i have to say I was most impressed by the amazing weather.
[02:45] Woman: Yeah, the weather there is amazing. Which of the sites listed as part of our official tour did you see, and of those, which was your favorite?
[02:54] Man: First I saw the theatre, which was beautifully designed.
[02:58] AUDIO: It was not nearly as cool as the Town Hall though - the building is a huge part of Melbourne’s history. Definitely my favorite. I saw the aquarium too, but wasn’t too impressed.
[03:10] Woman: I see. Yes, people often have great reviews of Town Hall. Now I would like to ask you about your dining experience.
[03:18] AUDIO: Did you enjoy the food there?
[03:20] Man: Absolutely - I love it!
[03:22] Woman: I’m glad to hear it. Could you tell me a little bit about what you most enjoyed about the food?
[03:27] Man: Being such an international city, I loved the variety - I could find any type of food I wanted.
[03:33] AUDIO: Whether I wanted seafood, burgers, or anything else, you name it and they had it.
[03:39] Woman: Did you drive to Melbourne?
[03:41] Man: No, I flew. I thought about going by train, but the interest of time I decided to go by plane.
[03:48] Woman: Right, I see. And would you mind telling me whether you are under 20, between the ages of 20 and 40, or older than 40?
[04:33] Man: Er, it would be nice if I were still under 20. My vacation probably would have been quite different.
[04:41] AUDIO: Actually though, I just turned 41 last week.
[04:44] Woman: Oh, happy birthday! So did you treat yourself and fly first class?
[04:49] Man: Ha! No way. I would love to have a budget that high. I’m more in the mid-range income level.
[04:56] AUDIO: I wasn’t always though - I spent much of my life in a low-income household.
[05:02] Woman: I see. That answers my next question then, of income level. And what was the purpose of this visit?
[05:09] Man: I had to go there on business a lot before and decided I would go there for tourism this time.
[05:15] Woman: I see. And what is your occupation?
[05:18] Man: I am mainly a computer programmer.
[05:20] AUDIO: I also write for a travel magazine on the side, which is why i visited Melbourne before, but it’s not my main source of income.
[05:28] Woman: I see. Wow, it sounds like you work a lot!
[05:32] Man: Yes, I am very busy, which is exactly why I took a nice week-long vacation to Melbourne.
[05:39] Woman: I completely agree. Would you care to comment on your accommodation?
[05:44] Man: My hotel was good value. Staying in the city can get really expensive, so it was nice to find such a good price for the location and quality.
[05:53] AUDIO: I’m glad I didn’t end up in some cheap motel in the middle of nowhere.
[05:58] Woman: I’m glad you didn’t either. Well, thank you for taking part in our survey, and I’m glad you enjoyed your vacation!
[06:05] Man: No problem. Take care!

passages.title: Improvement Plan
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "Improvement Plan"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:54] AUDIO: Thank you all for coming to our community meeting. As you know, we are excited to unveil our improvement plan as we look forward to the influx of tourists in the summer months. I’ll start with a quick overview of the main points of interest in the area for anyone who may not quite know his or her way around yet, and then I’ll get into the improvements made. First off is my favorite, the Science Museum, which is on the corner of Saint George Road.

[01:21] AUDIO: If you have not visited it yet, I encourage you to go before the busy season. It is absolutely spectacular - there is even a flight simulator you can try out! Just west of the Science Museum is the National History Museum. It’s a site not to be missed as well, with each floor devoted to a different era in our nation’s history.

[01:43] AUDIO: There are special exhibits for children with interactive games and fun history lessons, too. If you’re looking for parking, it is available on the intersection of Queen Street and South King Street in the Car Park. Standard hourly and daily rates do apply. The best place for souvenirs is the Shopping Mall, though it gets extremely busy during peak times.

[02:06] AUDIO: You can get there from the tube, or the entrance on Timber Road, just south of Cornwell Road. This area has students everywhere, usually from the Primary School across the street from the Shopping Mall. Classes often take field trips and engage in guided tours through the area. So that’s the overview of the main sites and hopefully by now I’ve given you a general idea of the area.

[03:07] AUDIO: Now I’m going to outline the improvements we have made in our efforts to make the experience even better for each and every one of our visitors. You probably noticed when you first drove into the Car Park this morning, that there is now additional signage to help avoid confusion. The directions were not entirely clear at first, so we have increased the number of one-way signs indicating the correct direction of traffic flow. Not far from there, in line with our mission of giving back to the community, we constructed a brand new playground for the Primary School.

[03:41] AUDIO: It is really something to be excited for - the equipment is state-of-the-art and includes swings, a small climbing wall, and even an obstacle course. Now we’ll head north and take a look at the Science Museum. In response to our feedback from past visitors to the museum, there is now free information available outlining not only upcoming IMAX showings, but also natural wonders like meteor showers, eclipses, and other cool natural events. The Science Museum isn’t the only Museum improving the experience of its visitors.

[04:19] AUDIO: The National History Museum has added an entire new wing to its facility to accommodate the large crowds of people gathering to see the Civil War exhibit, inventions timeline exhibit, and other wonderful sections of the museum. The increase in space will definitely give a more calm, comfortable experience for visitors. And finally, remember when there was actually a line at the mall entrance from the Tube Station? It was terrible trying to get anywhere from the Tube because foot traffic got so backed up sometimes.

[04:54] AUDIO: We have addressed that by adding another entry point into the mall from the other end of the platform to disperse the crowd. So those are the major improvements we have made. Clearly having too many people that want to visit and enjoy what our community has to offer the public is a good problem to have, and I am confident that we have made the changes necessary to accommodate the growing interest in the area. As always, we welcome any questions, comments, or concerns about the new improvements plan.

[05:25] AUDIO: In a few minutes I will open up the floor for questions but you can also contact me or any other board member by email or through the city website. Thank you for coming, and I now encourage you to stay for the Questions and Answers panel occurring between now and 10.30...

passages.title: Project Assignments
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 3: "Project Assignments"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:59] Tutor: So you were both given your project assignments for your senior thesis today right?
[01:04] Jane: Yes, and we already have to submit our topics next week!
[01:08] Mark: But how could they give us a grade this soon?
[01:11] Tutor: No, next week’s due date will not be counted towards your final grade.
[01:15] AUDIO: The teachers are just going to read your topic and give you feedback.
[01:19] Jane: Oh, I see. So first we should come up with our topics, and then what?
[01:24] Tutor: Well, once you know what you want to study, you need to think about how you’ll study it.
[01:30] AUDIO: You need to decide on your research methods. The methods will be the main part of your paper.
[01:35] Mark: What about the results section?
[01:37] Tutor: Well, I can give you feedback on that, but you will be the one carrying out an experiment and thus will have to produce the results on your own.

[01:47] AUDIO: What I would like to do today is practise writing research papers before you even begin your reports. I’ll give you samples of old data from past experience, and you can practice writing results and drawing conclusions.
[02:02] Jane: I think that would be really helpful.
[02:04] Mark: Yeah, it sounds like a lot of extra work, but I’m sure it will make our actual project easier.
[02:10] Tutor: You exactly right. So let’s get started. First, let’s try this simple experiment on fruit flies.
[02:17] AUDIO: Read the information, and then take 25 minutes to summarise a results and conclusion section. That’s really important - pay attention to the time limit.
[02:27] Jane: OK, does it still have to be 6,000 words?
[02:30] Tutor: No, don’t worry about that
[02:32] Mark: What if we get off topic?
[02:34] Tutor: I wouldn’t worry too much - you will have so much information to write about that it should be easy to stay on topic.
[03:19] Jane: But what about other sources?
[03:20] Tutor: Well for this assignment, you can use the one from your textbook.
[03:25] AUDIO: In your actual paper, you should find old experiments that support your topic.
[03:30] Mark: So do we need to find different types of sources? For instance, should I be conducting lots of interviews to use in my paper?
[03:39] Tutor: No, there’s no need to conduct lots of interviews or anything like that.
[03:44] Mark: OK, I’m ready to get started. I’m still a little confused though, on how we should format our paper.
[03:50] Tutor: Don’t worry about it for now, but on your final paper, make sure to pay attention to the format. It should follow the guidelines exactly.
[04:00] Jane: Oh man, I’m starting to understand why they give us all semester to do this.
[04:05] AUDIO: Are there any other small details like that that we should know about?
[04:09] Tutor: Not a whole lot, make sure you provide two copies - one for your teacher of course, but one for yourself as well.
[04:17] AUDIO: And of course, you know the due date, right?
[04:20] Mark: Uh, it’s April 11, right?
[04:22] Jane: What? No! It’s May 11. Right?
[04:26] Tutor: Yes. The due date is May 11. Write it down!
[04:31] Mark: Oh wow. Yeah, I need to note it. Also, I’m having trouble finding information on my topic. What if i can’t find enough good sources?
[04:39] Tutor: It’s alright to change your topic. Just make sure to do it before the beginning of April.
[04:45] Mark: Oh really? Wow, I’m definitely going to change it then.
[04:48] Tutor: Just make sure to write a note to your teacher letting him or her know.
[04:53] Jane: Okay. So getting back to writing this sample paper, where do we start? Should I just explain the experiment and what happened?
[05:01] Tutor: Well, you need to start with your hypothesis - what you think will happen - and then describe your procedure.
[05:08] AUDIO: Then you can write up the results and your conclusions.
[05:12] Jane: Oh boy, I don’t know if I can handle any more instructions…

content: 📌 Advertising Effect

Methods of communication

Effect on your product salesThe customer's [ _____ ] after he or she experiences the ad is most important.Marketing strategiesOn international flights, it is wise for advertisements to be displayed in the common [ _____ ] of most passengersVery few young people buy [ _____ ]The UNESCO website would be a good place to advertise for companies aiming to improve the [ _____ ]One good location to place ads for sunscreen is the [ _____ ]A good scene for a water purification commercial would be[ _____ ]
transcript: [01:10] AUDIO: Hello class, and welcome back to Marketing Strategies. This week I will expand upon last week’s lecture by talking about factors you should consider when creating advertising materials and the effects they can have on your product sales. Lesson one: limit your advertising to the geographic area of your target market. Though you may have a product that people want in a large area, the distance that customers are willing to travel is a significant factor in their choice of where to purchase that product.

[01:46] AUDIO: Take this example - if you are really hungry and decide you want a burrito, would you choose the restaurant that is a block from your apartment, or the one that is just as good - or even slightly better - across town? Of course you’ll pick the closer restaurant. Next, there’s the method of communication to your target market. How do you decide among radio ads, TV commercials, fliers, or even word of mouth?

[02:15] AUDIO: While we often think of the visual presentation of ads, there is much more to advertising than the look. Studies show that consumers are much more likely to remember advertising slogans if there is also a sound played. Did you know that your sense of smell is closely linked with memory? Think about Mandy’s Candy Store up the road.

[02:38] AUDIO: Every time you walk past it, you can just smell the chocolate, right? I bet you can almost smell it now. Just mentioning the name brings about the smell memory, and in turn a chocolate craving. What better way to sell chocolate bars?

[02:55] AUDIO: Obviously sometimes appealing to the senses isn’t the most practical way to advertise. For example, it is a good idea to come up with a marketing strategy that adapts to the product, especially digital products. The flexibility of this kind of product is extremely important, so it is very common for advertisers to form one single layout for all of their ads - the visual, the medium, even the majority of the content - and simply update the ad each time they come out with a new version. Remember, advertising is all about stirring up the right feeling in your potential customers, whether by stimulating the senses, appealing to intellect, and so on.

[03:41] AUDIO: Once the customer experiences the ad, the important thing is his or her reaction. Some could love the ad you made, but unless he or she considers buying the product, you have failed to get the reaction you were looking for. So once you have successfully reached your target customer and you have his or her business, often you will want to expand to a larger market. More often than not, the same marketing strategies you used in your small campaign may not work for a larger audience.

[04:18] AUDIO: The larger you scale your product, the more factors you must consider. For instance, Apple operates worldwide, so they must tailor their advertising for each market they enter. Often you’ll see Apple ads on international flights that appear not only in English, which is the lingua franca of most regions, but also in the native language of the majority of passengers. I traveled to Russia last week, and it was really interesting to see the same Nike ad that I have seen a hundred times - except this time it was in Russian!

[04:56] AUDIO: Okay, going back to the medium of the advertisement, even after choosing to create print ads (instead of radio announcements, television commercials, etc) there is more to consider. If you print your ad in a newspaper, it will be read by a far different audience than if you print your ad in a popular magazine. Would you put an ad for the new Justin Bieber album in a newspaper? Probably not, because that product is most suitable for youths.

[05:25] AUDIO: Let’s face it - do you know anyone under the age of 25 that buys a newspaper? No! Now let’s try a few strategy exercises. Imagine you are a company that is aiming to improve the environment by making products that reduce human waste. How would you advertise your product?

[05:46] AUDIO: Clearly it would send the wrong message if you put up fliers or other material that causes lots of waste paper. [06:14] AUDIO: Alright, one last thing. Let’s say you’re filming a commercial for a water filter pitcher. What would be good scenery to use for the background? [06:39] AUDIO: So to wrap things up today, think about the geography of your target market, the type of marketing you should use, and the most effective wat to appeal to the customer in order to make a successful ad campaign. transcript: [02:08] Employer: Hello, is this John Murphy?
[02:10] Applicant: Hi, yes it is.
[02:11] Employer: Hi John, this is Ed Heisenburg from the Wild Dunes Spa and Resort calling about your application for our lifeguard position. Do you have a few minutes to talk?
[02:22] Applicant: Yes, absolutely
[02:23] Employer: Great. Could you give me your address?
[02:25] Applicant: Sure. My address is 45 Elsinore Court.
[02:30] Employer: I’m sorry, was that Eleanor? Could you spell that for me?
[02:33] Applicant: Sure - it’s Elsinore. E-L-S-I-N-O-R-E.
[02:39] Employer: Okay, thanks. And is this the number we should reach you at in the future? 099885767?
[02:46] Applicant: No, this is my home phone, but let me give you my mobile phone number instead: 077896245. Call me on that one.
[02:56] Employer: Okay - I’ll make a note of that. Could you tell me your availability?
[03:00] Applicant: Sure. I am usually available during afternoons or weekends. I would prefer not to be scheduled on weeknights because I work part-time as a waiter.
[03:09] Employer: That shouldn’t be a problem, since we don’t stay open very late anyway. And do you have any other employment experience?
[03:16] Applicant: Yes, I have worked at a few other places. I was the baseball coach at Ridgemont High School last season.
[03:23] Employer: I see. And do you have any other experience that you would like us to note on your application?
[03:29] Applicant: Yes. Last year I worked at the beach as a rescue diver.
[03:33] Employer: Rescue diver? That sounds intense!
[03:36] Applicant: Well, it’s really just like being a lifeguard, except in the ocean instead of a pool. So kind if like being a lifeguard at the world’s largest pool.
[03:45] Employer: Haha. I see. So could you tell me about the relevant skills you have? I’m guessing a lot, given your experience.
[04:27] Applicant: I am CPR certified and have 2 years of diving experience.
[04:31] Employer: Great! It sounds like you are well qualified for this position. When does your CPR certification expire?
[04:38] Applicant: Hm. I think in November, but let me quickly check my CPR card… actually, it expires in October.
[04:47] Employer: Okay, so regardless you have it through the end of the summer. When is your ideal time to work?
[04:53] Applicant: Since I work in the restaurant on weeknights, I like weekends best - specifically Saturday mornings.
[05:00] Employer: I see. We do already have a lot of staff available on Saturdays, but I do need an early morning shift lifeguard. How early could you work Saturday morning?
[05:11] Applicant: I can get there by 6.00 if need be.
[05:15] Employer: You’ll be happy to know we open a little later than that, but I’ll put you down for Saturday morning here.
[05:21] Applicant: Oh awesome! I can’t wait to get started.
[05:24] Employer: How about you come in next Saturday, the 12th?
[05:27] Applicant: That sounds good.
[05:28] Employer: Great - We can figure out other shifts for you to work when you come in then. One last thing - just out of curiosity, where did you hear about us?
[05:37] Applicant: I heard your ad on the radio while I was driving this morning.
[05:41] Employer: You know, I think you’re the first person who has responded to our radio ads. It’s almost always people who have seen us in the newspaper.
[05:49] Applicant: Yeah, I don’t have time to read through the newspaper every morning. I have plenty of time in the car to listen to radio ads.
[05:56] Employer: That makes sense. Well, thanks for your time, and we’ll look forward to seeing you on the 12th.

passages.title: Free Class About Safety Around Campus
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "Free Class About Safety Around Campus"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:55] Geoffrey: Good evening, I’m Geoffrey Miller, from the University of Nottingham Student Union. And in this week’s free class, Carlos Garcia is going to tell us about safety around campus. Over to you, Carlos.

[01:08] Carlos: Thank you, Geoffrey. And thank you for all of your attendance today. Also, I would like to thank the student union here at the university for organising this lecture. Well, I have been serving and protecting the city of Nottingham for over 20 years now as a member of the police department. Does anyone know what type of crime is the most prevalent on campus? I heard someone say drugs and alcohol - that’s actually isn’t too much of an issue.

[01:35] Carlos: Violence? Nope. Actually, the biggest thing we worry about here is theft. The nature of crime on Nottingham’s campus is quite different from that of the surrounding areas. Crime rates across the East Midlands are very difficult to control. We would like to see the rate stay the same for this calendar year, but it has been increasing steadily over the past three years. On campus, however, I’m happy to say that the overall crime rate has fallen this year.

[02:04] Carlos: You wouldn’t think so if you have seen the extremely exaggerated stories in the media. The media has done nothing but cause more concern about crime in our area. Even the crime shows you see today are a little bit far fetched, but at least viewers know they are not real events. We would really like to see more factual news articles out there so the public can have a rational sense of the safety level of our society.

[03:06] Carlos: OK, let’s move on to what to do when you see a crime. Do not get involved if at all possible, and do not draw too much attention to yourself by running away in a conspicuous manner. Though most likely (and hopefully) you will not have to experience this situation, if you are being mugged please do not try to resist. Instead, be compliant and seek help after the incident.

[03:32] Carlos: Like I said, though, it is highly unlikely that you will find yourself amidst a crime, but it is important to be prepared should it ever happen. We find that educating students and staff on the correct precautions to take is the best way to increase your safety. Just remember to be smart when you’re out late at night, and avoid any area or person that looks suspicious. I know it sounds obvious but I cannot stress this enough. It is also not a bad idea to have your mobile phone with you at all times, but be careful.

[04:08] Carlos: If you are chatting on your smartphone on your way home, you are a prime target for thieves. I’d like to see a show of hands - how many people have left work or the library after 10 p.m to go home before? A lot of you, right? If you do have to go home late at night, please don’t walk home alone. More often than not there is someone there that will be walking the same direction as you at some point.

[04:36] Carlos: Walk home with a friend or coworker. Even if you must use your phone to call someone that is nearby to walk with you, it is always safer to walk home with someone. So when you’re walking home, you may feel more comfortable with some sort of self-defense, such as pepper spray. Now it’s your call whether you want to carry something like this or not. However, I absolutely advise against carrying a knife or any other offensive weapon. All too often they can be used against you if you are disarmed, putting yourself in more dagger.

[05:15] Carlos: For all those interested, the recreation centre offers a free self-defense class to all students every Thursday evening. While obviously an introductory self-defense class may not equip you to fight off villains like a regular superhero, it does come in handy sometimes. After taking a self-defense class, you will surely be more aware of possible dangers and how to deal with them. So hopefully now you have a more complete understanding of the nature of crimes committed on your campus, and how to avoid being a victim.

[05:48] Carlos: I know most students at the University of Nottingham are not the criminal types, but remember that there is no barrier like a wall or something keeping non-students out. There is no army force securing the borders, and I doubt anyone wants it that way. The campus is generally a safe place, but it is not immune to small crimes once in a while. Alright. That’s all I have to say for today. Stay safe!

passages.title: Giving A Speech
content: 📌 GIVING A SPEECH
Reason for nervousness
Lecturers often feel more [ _____ ] if the speech is importantMany think that the ability to make a good public speaking is [ _____ ], while in fact it is a skill that can be learned by anyone.
How to prepare a quality speech

The audience will only remember the [ _____ ] sentence of a speechEnsure that your speech is [ _____ ]Do’s and Don’ts❌ Don’t start your speech until audience is [ _____ ].✅ You can make your main ideas or notes on cards or a [ _____ ].❌ You do not need to write down the [ _____ ] speech.✅ You can just write [ _____ ] ideas.✅ Remember to [ _____ ] yourself to see how long your speech will be.❌ Don’t just read a [ _____ ].
transcript: [01:03] AUDIO: Good morning. Today I am going to cover the daunting task of giving a quality speech - a thought that makes most of us cringe. In fact, 90% of all people feel nervous about public speaking, about 10% of whom are described as genuinely terrified. Hopefully when we are finished here today, you all will be in the 10% of the population who do not feel nervous at all. Did you know that lecturers tend to get more nervous if the speech they are giving is an important one? It makes sense, right?

[01:35] AUDIO: You probably wouldn’t be nearly as nervous to address your residence hall about the proper use of the recycle and compost bins as you might be if you were asked to give the graduation speech to your entire 5000-student class. So what is it that makes some people completely comfortable in front of crowds? Some people think that the ability to give a good speech is a gift that others are simply born with. This is almost never the case. Public speaking can be learned with practice. The first, most important thing you can do to improve your confidence in delivering a speech is to prepare a quality speech.

[02:11] AUDIO: Honestly, while the content of your speech is relatively important, the audience will really only remember the last sentence you say. It is a good idea to structure the rest of your speech to lead up to this last point to really drive your message home. This is a good way to ensure that your speech is well-organized. Once you are confident in the quality of the speech you have written, the rest is just about your stage presence.

[02:41] AUDIO: Let’s go through some do’s and don’ts of public speaking. First, you want to command the attention of the room. Do not - I repeat, do not proceed with your speech until the audience is paying attention. Even Martin Luther King, Junior’s I Have a Dream speech wouldn’t have made any difference in the world without the undivided attention of his audience. To continue with the I Have a Dream example, one of the reasons that MLK was such an effective orator was his ability to speak with passion and engage with his audience.

[03:14] AUDIO: That sort of charisma does not come from reading straight from paper. Don’t get me wrong - it is a good idea to write your main ideas down on a note card, sheet of paper, or something. But one factor that will consistently lead to a boring, forgettable speech is writing down your entire speech. Do not write your full speech down.

[03:35] AUDIO: If you are constantly reading your paper, you are not making eye contact with your audience, and thus failing to really express the feeling that goes with your ideas. I advise you to write one or two ideas, so if you suddenly draw a blank you have something to jog your memory. If you’ve written a good speech that you believe in, those ideas should be sufficient to keep you on track. Once you have those ideas written down, give your speech a few practice runs in front of the mirror, into your sound recorder on your phone, or with a friend before it comes time to address a crowd.

[04:11] AUDIO: That way you can hear how the ideas come across, make sure there are no abrupt transitions, and find out whether you’re talking too fast or too slow. Timing is important - make sure you time yourself beforehand to see how long your speech is. That is pretty much it! With practice you’ll be able to deliver an expert speech that engages and even maybe inspires your audience. Just remember - speak with emotion. No one wants to listen to someone reading from a script.

[04:41] AUDIO: As I come to a close in my speech, I’ll point out that I have employed all of these tips that I have covered. I practiced my speech ahead of time and timed it, and I can even show you my one small index card with just three simple bullets on it. It’s as easy as that!

transcript: [01:52] Police: Hello, London Police Department
[01:54] Anna: Yes, I would like to report a robbery
[01:56] Police: Alright, just a minute while I pull up the form. OK, could you give me your first and last name?
[02:01] Anna: Anna Grieg.
[02:02] Police: Anna, Greg? G-R-E-G?
[02:06] Anna: No, Grieg. G-R-I-E-G.
[02:09] Police: Got it. Alright moving on: gender - female. Date of birth?
[02:13] Anna: 15th of March, 1980
[02:15] Police: Alright, thanks. Just a few more personal information questions and then we can address your claim.
[02:22] Anna: Alright
[02:23] Police: What is the address?
[02:25] Anna: 4 Ellendale St. That’s E-L-L-E-N-D-A-L-E
[02:31] Police: Oh right, Ellendale Street. Yeah we’ve had a lot of break-ins in that area lately. And the postal code?
[02:38] Anna: W52AT
[02:40] Police: And are you a citizen of the UK?
[02:43] Anna: No
[02:43] Police: Okay, what type of citizenship do you have?
[02:47] Anna: Well, I lived in the United States for most of my life, but I am actually of Grenadian nationality.
[02:53] Police: Okay, so is that the country that issued your passport?
[02:58] Anna: Yes.
[02:58] Police: Alright. And what is the crime you are reporting?
[03:35] Anna: I already said - a robbery!
[03:37] Police: Oh, right. Sorry, this is about the hundredth robbery report I’ve filled out today. Have you had any prior break-ins?
[03:44] Anna: Um, in the building or just my flat? The unit below mine got broken into last year.
[03:50] Police: No, just your flat.
[03:52] Anna: Oh - then no. Not here.
[03:54] Police: Alright, let’s see here. Can you think of anything that was out of the ordinary around your building, or anyone who may have had reason to do this?
[04:04] Anna: No, it seemed like just a normal evening. I didn’t see anyone suspicious, and can’t think of anyone that would target me specifically.
[04:12] Police: How long has this been your place of residence?
[04:15] Anna: Hm, let me think. I moved in on February 1, and it’s October, so it’s been about 8 months already. Wow, time flies!
[04:24] Police: And that is just Ellendale, yeah?
[04:27] Anna: Yes. I have lived in the UK for just over one year.
[04:31] Police: I see. Can you give me the first and last name of all members of the household?
[04:35] Anna: Actually, I live alone.
[04:37] Police: OK - so no other occupants. And can you give me a brief account of what happened?
[04:42] Anna: I left to go to a dinner party at 6 p.m, and when I returned at 11 I found the place ransacked and a lot of my things gone.
[04:50] Police: Any sign of forced entry?
[04:52] Anna: Yes, the back door was wide open, and it looked like someone used a crowbar to force it open.
[04:57] Police: I see. And just to be clear, was the door locked when you left?
[05:01] Anna: Of course!
[05:02] Police: Hey, you would be surprised how many reports we get where people have failed to lock their doors. Now I need you to list any missing items valued above £200.
[05:14] Anna: So far I’m missing my computer, my purse with my wallet in it, and the TV.
[05:20] Police: OK, Let’s start with the computer. What is the estimated value?
[05:26] Police: And what is the serial number?
[05:31] Police: Thank you, and a visual description?
[05:33] Anna: It is a black 13-inch Pemdas Cloudbook. There is an Oxford sticker on the lid.
[05:38] Police: OK, and could you give a description of the purse?
[05:42] Anna: Sure. It’s a Claude Frieda shoulder bag and the material is silver-colored cloth.
[05:48] Police: Price?
[05:50] Police: Okay. That concludes my report. I’ll submit it and we’ll let you know of any developments.

transcript: [00:55] Tutor: Hi, Mark. Hi, Gina. What can I help you with?
[00:58] Mark: So we were hoping you could help us with this extracurricular project.
[01:03] Tutor: Sure - what is the topic?
[01:05] Gina: Attending business school.
[01:07] Tutor: This sounds like a great idea. So you’re going to explain the requirements for getting into business school?
[01:13] Mark: Not exactly. It will be more broadly about the experience - the academics, accommodation, and social experience that comes with being a part of business school.
[01:24] Tutor: I see. So would your audience be the general public?
[01:29] Gina: Well, we would probably want more to focus on members of the institution - we would especially like to reach individual applicants to the business school.

[01:37] Tutor: I see. Now what form will this information be? You could give a talk to all the summer courses - all you would need is permission from the course director. Or you could pass out information outside the student union.
[01:52] Mark: Those are both good ideas. What about sending out pamphlets in the mail?
[01:56] Tutor: Most college students never check their mail. Maybe you could make a video and show it on campus?
[02:02] Gina: That’s a great idea. We’ll do the video
[02:05] Tutor: Great. And as members of the business school, do you have an incentive to attract new students? If so, this idea is a great way to do that.
[02:15] Mark: No, the idea actually came about because of how much students like us worry about their studies.

[02:22] Gina: Yeah - when I got into business school, there were a lot of things I had not prepared for, so the video would cover a lot of things Mark and I wish we had known upon entering business school.
[02:32] Tutor: Right. What would you talk about first?
[03:10] Mark: The first and probably most important section would be academics.
[03:13] Tutor: Good idea. So would you provide guidance on what courses to take?

[03:18] Gina: We want to focus especially on the approaches professors take - their teaching methods. It is far different than what students are used to in high school, and even in liberal arts college.
[03:29] Tutor: Good idea. And how long do you think you would spend explaining academics?
[03:35] Mark: We’ll probably spend 7 minutes on it
[03:37] Gina: We also have some ideas for talking about housing, food options, and stuff like that. We’re not really sure how to tie it all together though.
[03:46] Tutor: I think it would be suitable to title that section accommodation - what do you think?

[03:51] Mark: That could work. We’ll definitely describe the different dining options at the cafeteria, and then walk students through flats and the grueling process of finding one near the business school campus.
[04:02] Gina: Okay - so we would cover specifics on the cafeteria, as well as flats?
[04:07] Mark: I think those are both helpful. We could spend about 6 minutes on accommodations, and be sure to touch on those specifically.
[04:14] Tutor: Great. Is there anything else you would talk about?
[04:18] Gina: We definitely want to go over the social aspect of attending school here
[04:23] Tutor: Of course. I think it’s good to have a little fun once in a while when you’re working so hard in school.
[04:29] Mark: I think we are going to introduce new students to the disco that so many upperclassmen know and love. Maybe we’ll include a few other places too, but that’s the main one.

[04:39] Gina: We’re also going to invite students to the international evening taking place in the first week of school as a great chance for our large international student population to meet a lot of other new students.
[04:51] Tutor: It can definitely be hard to meet people as an international student. I think that is a great idea. You may want to spend slightly longer on this section than the other two.
[05:02] Mark: Hm… how about 8 minutes?
[05:05] Gina: That sounds reasonable. So overall, the introduction should take 3 minutes, and then the conclusion should take 4, giving us a total of 28 minutes.

[05:16] Tutor: I wouldn’t rush your introduction. Maybe give it between 4 and 6 minutes. The conclusion, though, can be shorter since it’s just a quick refresher of each of the topics. Give that not more than 2 minutes.
[05:33] Mark: Okay. So in total the video should take about the same time, just more into and less conclusion?
[05:40] Gina: Precisely. Alright - we are going to get to work on our video. Thanks for your help!

passages.title: Research Project
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 3: "Research Project"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:55] Dani: So tell me about your research project, John
[00:59] John: I created a questionnaire for the study to determine people’s opinions of the relative feasibility of earning a living in Brisbane.
[01:07] Dani: Oh, cool. How is it scored? Are they all multiple choice questions?

[01:12] John: Well, the questions consist primarily of yes/no responses. There are two free response questions at the end. Participants will use a computer to fill in their answer; that way it is really easy to analyse the data afterward.
[01:28] Dani: Great! It sounds like you have a pretty solid idea of what you should do. Just don't forget to submit a copy of your plans to Professor Curran by the 15th.
[01:39] John: Oh, I almost forgot!
[01:41] Dani: Hm, you don’t do it for high grade or praise, but he can review and give you feedback.
[01:47] John: Right, that will be helpful - he has been conducting studies like this for 30 years now.
[01:54] Dani: Yep, oh and I’m curious - are you going to be in the room giving subjects directions for the questionnaire?

[02:01] John: Well, I think the instructions will be provided by another representative who will not be analysing the data. I want them to feel they can answer and be completely anonymous, so I will not be in the room. Anonymity is really important for this study.

[02:17] Dani: I agree. Good idea. You should tell the representative to remind subjects to fully consider both sides of each issue. Sometimes it’s really easy to immediately check “yes” or “no” without stopping to think about it completely.
[02:34] John: That’s so true! It’s like a race to finish the questionnaire first or something. I’ll make sure to include that in the instructions. This report has to be perfect!
[02:45] Dani: Wow, what’s the big deal? I know it’s part of your grade and all…
[02:51] John: Well it’s that, but also a well-executed study could grab the attention of faculty in the department, which would be a huge deal.
[02:59] Dani: So… for attention?
[03:01] John: No silly! I mean I could really gain the respect of professors who may later take me on as a graduate student in their labs.
[03:09] Dani: Oh, I see. Let me take a look at the survey. Wow, this looks great! The map of the median income by region is a great tool - where did you find it?

[03:57] John: Well thanks! I read a lot of sources and just noticed this one in a small psychology journal called Modern Psychology. It’s more helpful than the photo I added, but I think the photo is just so interesting. It was in the newspaper last year during that huge wage strike.
[04:14] Dani: It’s great. Probably not necessary, but it looks great. I don’t understand - what is WKRX’s involvement here?
[04:23] John: Oh - the radio station agreed to sponsor the study if I play their station in the room.
[04:29] Dani: Wow, interesting. So you don’t have to pay for any of this?
[04:34] John: Exactly.
[04:35] Dani: Nice! Where did you get that idea?
[04:37] John: Last month at the Psychology Club Council meeting someone talked about how easy it is to get sponsorship from local businesses, so I listened to their advice and called around!
[04:48] Dani: I’ll have to remember that. Well, this all looks great. Good luck!

passages.title: The Pleasanton Town Market
content: Research MethodsObjectsProblemsReference section[ _____ ]There is too much information[ _____ ]RebellionBias makes it[ _____ ][ _____ ]Jim WileyThe information is insufficientNewspaper archives[ _____ ]More detail is needed
transcript: [01:03] AUDIO: Good afternoon. In the last few lectures we’ve been covering the social and political pressures that influenced the rise of the rebellion of 1679. Today I would like to focus on the Pleasanton Town Market. Now, why are we talking all about some market? It’s not like it was the first market ever, or even a particular large market. The Pleasanton Town Market is important because it is often mentioned in the literature found in the library. If you have ever been there, you have probably seen all of the hand-crafted items sold there now. But what was originally bought and sold in the town market? In the beginning, the market sold products such as meats, furs, and simple tools. Overtime, though, it became known as the place to find quality livestock. People came from all over the world to find the biggest and best cows, pigs, and chickens. In fact, the profits from the Town Market became the savior of a plummeting economy during a time of much turmoil. Not to be confused with the reconstruction era, a period of rapid development came about in the 1660’s as a result of the market’s vendors contributing their profits to building up much needed public facilities and defense, which would later make a huge impact on the outcome of the war.

[02:23] AUDIO: For many years, the market flourished and began to draw in large tourism crowds in addition to the throngs of livestock customers. However, as revolutions in farming came about, more people moved to farms far from the city centre. Customers grew more and more reluctant to travel all the way to the town centre for their meats when they could easily choose to buy from local farmers near them for a fraction of the price. With such a fall in the profits of the town’s major profit generator, some quality town planning was needed. In the mayoral election of 1668, a young man of little fame just barely claimed the popular vote - none other than the now legendary John C.Wiley. Wiley’s first decision as mayor of Pleasanton was to deal with the quickly failing Town Market. The building with the large clock was a landmark that had symbolised growth in Pleasanton for a generation. Wiley decided to use the notoriety of the Town Market to set an example. During the historical Rotterdam Rebellion, Wiley gave all those involved lifetime prison sentences in the very same building. It stayed a prison for about 50 more years until they transported all remaining prisoners to other facilities and turned it into the historical monument today.

[03:46] AUDIO: Now that you know the basics of the history of the Pleasanton Town Market, I will introduce your next group project. I want you to make a short film based on the real historical events that occurred in Pleasanton before and during the uprising. I will give you some class time to look through the library’s reference section, but you will be responsible for conducting further research outside of class. I suggest starting by looking for information on the market itself. You’ll find plenty of information - in fact, some students complain that there is actually too much information on it. On your own time, you could find family members of old war veterans to conduct interviews. Sometimes they provide wonderful insight that you wouldn’t find in proper history books, but be careful - an interview that is riddled with bias is useless. I myself have some very old photographs here that you are welcome to take a look at for some inspiration. I’m lucky enough to own this one of Jim Wiley himself! Very interesting to see, but does not provide enough information to add much to film.

[04:51] AUDIO: Feel free to take this film into whatever direction you choose. You could even do a crime thriller based on real outlaws. All you would have to do is look through the newspaper archives in the crime section during that time period. Try to get as much detail as you can, but you may end up having to draw your own conclusions. Okay, that’s enough from me, so let’s go on to...

content:
Example
The discussion topic:Answer
lease for next yearThe total rent:Peter £110 & Jim £ [ _____ ]Car parking:in the[ _____ ]A place to buy things:[ _____ ], because Jim works thereThe fees they should share:[ _____ ]feesThe appliances needed:- The landlord will provide the microwave
- The[ _____ ] is needed in the kitchen
- Peter will bring some dining room and living room furniture
- Jim will buy a [ _____ ] at the storeLocation of the telephone:in the [ _____ ]Move-in date:[ _____ ]Watching the game together:on [ _____ ]What Jim needs to do before move-in:take[ _____ ] in the morning
transcript: [01:57] Peter: Hey Jim, it’s Peter.
[01:58] Jim: Oh hey Peter. What’s up?
[01:59] Peter: I thought I’d call so we could hammer out the details for next year’s lease.
[02:04] Jim: That’s a good idea. Did we ever decide on how to split the total rent?
[02:09] Peter: Well, I was thinking since my room is bigger I probably should pay a little more, so I could pay £110 and you could pay £80. Does that sound okay?

[02:21] Jim: Considering that my old apartment cost me £100 for a smaller room, I’m definitely alright with that! Hey, I was looking at a map of the area, and can’t seem to find a bus stop near it. Do you know where we would catch the bus?
[02:36] Peter: Well, the bus is actually pretty far from us, but we have that garage that we can park out cars in.

[02:43] Jim: Wow, that’s great! Convenient parking is hard to find, so we’re lucky we have that. Okay, so we have a whole lot of things we’ll need to buy when we move in - how do you want to split that up?
[02:55] Peter: I was wondering - do you still work at the supermarket?
[02:59] Jim: Yep, every Tuesday and Saturday.
[03:01] Peter: Would you be able to buy things from there if I send you a shopping list?
[03:07] Jim: Sure, I can do that.
[03:08] Peter: Great. Then I can take care of whatever else we need that you wouldn’t get at a supermarket. If you want, I’ll pick you up from work that day and we can go to the apartment together.
[03:21] Jim: That would be great, thanks.
[03:23] Peter: No problem - that way we can split the cost of petrol.
[03:27] Jim: Works for me. It’s so expensive these days, isn’t it?
[03:31] Peter: It’s downright obscene.
[04:08] Jim: So let’s figure out what appliances we need. Do we have a microwave?
[04:12] Peter: Yes, the landlord’s providing that for us. Hey, do you still have that space heater though? We need one for the kitchen since it’s not connected to the central heating.
[04:22] Jim: Oh, right, I’ll bring that. Anything else?
[04:24] Peter: Well, I have some dining room and living room furniture I can bring, so that should take care of most of the big stuff. You know what we do need though? Could you bring a toaster?
[04:35] Jim: I actually don’t have one. It doesn’t come with the microwave?
[04:39] Peter: No, the landlord is only supplying the microwave. It would really help if you could bring one.
[04:46] Jim: Okay, I’ll pick one up at the store. You know, I also have this cool antique rotary phone that would be a cool addition to the apartment. Sort of as decoration and utility.
[04:57] Peter: Oh cool! The only thing is, we’d have to put it in the kitchen, unless you want it in your room.
[05:04] Jim: Why not put it in the living room?

[05:06] Peter: The living room is too loud to have a phone conversation. The noise sort of carries, so if one person is trying to watch TV or have friends over the person on the phone won’t be able to hear.
[05:19] Jim: Hm, okay, well I guess kitchen it is then. Any other big things we need? That seems like everything
[05:27] Peter: That’s all I can think of. And of course, move-in is
[05:32] Jim: June 1st. I can’t wait. We’ll be able to watch the big game in our new apartment - it’s going to be awesome!
[05:39] Peter: Yeah, we can move in in the morning and then Friday night we can sit back and cheer on Liverpool.
[05:46] Jim: I have an exam in the morning, but will be done around 11 a.m. and can move in after. Wait...  Liverpool? You’re joking, right? I thought you were a Manchester United fan?
[05:56] Peter: MAN U? No way! Liverpool all the way!
[06:00] Jim: Oh no. I don’t know if I can live with a Liverpool fan...

passages.title: Earn And Learn Company
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "Earn And Learn Company"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:57] AUDIO: Welcome to all of you… Can everybody see and hear me?... Good… I’m Sarah Conor, an HR representative of Earn and Learn. I have been asked today to talk to you about our company. So, for those of you who don’t know very much about the company, let me start by giving you some basic information about it. Earn and Learn started nearly twenty years ago. It is not a charity but a for-profit company that enables promising entrepreneurs to make money while traveling. During the past ten years, it has grown rapidly and has gained great influence in most countries of the world. We have a partnership with the school and take a large number of recent graduates from the business school. So if you are a recent graduate I’d say you can consider applying to our company. Before your application, you might be curious about what sort of places you could go to. There are four main locations, but you also have the freedom to submit a different location and if they can make the necessary arrangements, you can go.

[02:02] AUDIO: The first country Earn and Learn established locations in was the U.S., where you may choose from multiple locations, as long as you can commit to their more rigid schedule of August to December. Also, you could do the Australia internship. That one is really cool - you work at a wildlife shelter and learn about the business practices of nonprofit organisations. You do have to be willing to commit 8 months for that one, through. Perhaps that’s a long time to be so far away, but I would say it is really an amazing opportunity. I don’t know whether some of you are in decent physical shape. If so, the South Africa internship is another exciting one - you learn a lot about sustainable farming - but you would be doing some of the manual labor involved in maintaining a farm. Indeed, it’s hard work, but I think you would definitely be able to do it. It may be wise to wait until after their summer is over so it's not so terribly hot.

[03:07] AUDIO: In addition, There is a most recent established location in India. This one gives you more of a study abroad feel, given that they arrange a host family for you to stay with. In the other locations, you live in an apartment with other interns, so this is definitely a unique experience. Regardless of where you go, at the end of the program you get a Global Traveling Certificate, as long as you can explain your experience. You can provide a written log of what you did. I recommend writing journal or blog entries about what you do everyday, or a weekly summary of each day. Of course you don’t have to write up a formal report or anything like that. And you need to apply for it once you have returned. Some students may want to know whether this is a paid internship. Actually you have to pay for the flight there yourself. But you have the opportunity to create your own small business, which could earn you money if it’s successful.

[04:45] AUDIO: So basically you pay for it all up front, but when you’re there you can find ways to make money. That is to say, you pay for two thirds of the cost up front as a deposit, and then give the final installment one month prior to your return Finally, I have to remind you that you need a health check before you go, to make sure you’re not going to spread any communicable diseases. In addition, before you go, you don’t have to attend any meetings or workshops. You’ll meet everyone you'll be working with once you get there. Okay, well, that’s all I’ve time for today. Thanks for listening and I’m happy to take any questions if you have them...

content: TopicInformation source[ _____ ]check at the [ _____ ]Views on [ _____ ]interview the manager of [ _____ ]Practice of [ _____ ]find relevant information from the [ _____ ]How to deliver the plan:as an [ _____ ]Date of giving the presentation:on [ _____ ]Schedule of items due:First Phase: [ _____ ]Final Phase: Group [ _____ ]
transcript: [00:59] Student: Hi, Professor Timmons? Do you have a few minutes? I was hoping to talk about what I missed on Thursday.
[01:05] Professor: Hello, come in. Sure, sit down. Could you tell me your name please?
[01:10] Student: Margaret, sir. Margaret Parkinson. I apologize for missing your class but I had to go to the hospital.
[01:17] Professor: I’m sorry to hear that! Everything is OK now though, I hope?
[01:21] Student: Yes, thanks.

[01:23] Professor: Glad to hear it. So on Thursday I outlined the research project that will account for 30% of your grade. All students will be divided into groups and will give a well-researched presentation to the class covering a specific topic relevant to student life.
[01:42] Student: Oh, that sounds interesting - can we choose just any topic that pertains to life as a student, like how to start your own student organization?

[01:51] Professor: Well, though I’m sure that would be an informative presentation, I have already chosen a list of topics which I will assign. As an example, I assigned one group the topic of student loans. They are to research not just the prevalence of students who have loans to pay for their tuition but information as to how best to manage these loans and possible scholarships that could alleviate some of the financial burden.
[02:21] Student: That one sounds particularly interesting to me - could I request that topic? I could easily find out a lot about it by stopping by the Finance Office on my way to class.
[02:31] Professor: Unfortunately, that one is already taken by another group. I have, however, assigned you to a group and given you all one of two choices.
[02:41] Student: Oh, I see. What are the choices?

[02:44] Professor: The first is discussing smoking. Trends in the number of student smokers compared with the general population, popular reasons students take up smoking, and more healthy alternatives to smoking.

[02:57] Student: Hm, that one could be interesting. I’m not a smoker myself, but will see what my group thinks. If we did choose this topic, we would rather not put our fellow students on the spot to interview them - Where else could we gather information?
[03:11] Professor: How about where the cigarettes are sold?
[03:14] Student: Oh, that’s a great idea. I could interview the manager of a supermarket and find out the average age of people buying cigarettes, or how much they buy, that sort of thing?
[03:24] Professor: Precisely.
[03:25] Student: Okay, I’ll keep that in mind. And what was the other topic?

[03:29] Professor: The other topic is the practice of natural medicine. It sounds far more specific than the others, but it is more an exercise of outlining a career path. If your group chooses this, you would cover the specifics of becoming a Doctor of Natural Medicine, how to become licensed to practice natural medicine, what the career outlook is, etc. you could find much of the information you need on this in the Careers Office.
[04:02] Student: Wow, That would be really helpful not just in learning about natural medicine, but in how to approach researching any career path.
[04:10] Professor: That’s the idea. I want groups to really think outside the box to find information on their topics. They should interview multiple sources.
[04:20] Student: Okay, now I think I have the general idea. When is the presentation due?
[05:02] Professor: I expect each group to send me an email attachment of the plan ahead of time - by October 10th - so that I can ensure that you are on the right track.
[05:16] Student: Oh, that’s actually really reassuring. I would hate to spend so much time on a presentation only to find we had taken it in the wrong direction! So when is the presentation?
[05:27] Professor: I let groups choose from the list of time slots I have between November 1st and November 5th.
[05:35] Student: Okay, how about the 3rd? I’ll have to check with my group, of course, but maybe we could write a tentative time?
[05:41] Professor: Sure, let me take a look. I’m actually booked completely through the 3rd and 4th now. How about sometime in the afternoon of the 5th?

passages.title: The Gherkin Building
content: 📌 THE GHERKIN BUILDING
Commissioned by: [ _____ ] firm called Foster and Partners.
The features of its appearance:

Its shape is like a [ _____ ].It can reduce the carbon [ _____ ] of the city.It lets [ _____ ] pass through the building, both reducing heating costs and brightening up the workspace.One false story claimed that the exterior of the building is partly made of [ _____ ].Architectural concept:
Links [ _____ ] with the workplace.Relies less on [ _____ ] for temperature control than other similar buildings.
The features of its interior:

The atria that let fresh air pass through the interior are known as [ _____ ].There is a place for entertainment called the[ _____ ]at the top of the building.The future of urban planning and architecture:

It is likely that the entire [ _____ ] will be designed with more similarly eco-friendly buildings in future.A new building will be constructed aiming to produce zero waste and remove carbon dioxide from us as much as possible.
transcript: [01:05] AUDIO: Today I’d like to tell you about how U.K architects are playing their part to address the issue of global warming. You have seen many of these iconic buildings while going about your everyday life, but you may not know how they are affecting your tomorrow. In 2003, construction was completed on the famous Swiss Re Building, or more informally called the Gherkin, a true masterpiece commissioned by the law offices of Foster and Partner. This is not the first ambitious endeavor of the film - they are renowned for their various philanthropic, environmental efforts. The Gherkin, with its cutting edge green initiative and sharp design, is gaining recognition as an icon in modern architecture. You can pick it out of the London skyline by its unorthodox cigar shape. While its appearance is the obvious attribute at which to marvel, there is far more to this building than meets the eye. And let’s face it - there’s a lot about this building that meets the eye. The building helps reduce the city’s carbon footprint in a number of ways.

[02:18] AUDIO: Just a quick note - in case you’re not familiar with the term ‘carbon footprint’, get used to it! It’s a buzzword you’ll hear relentlessly to talk about reducing emissions. Think of it as the amount of harmful greenhouse gases that are given off into the environment by a single person, organisation, or product. So going back to the Gherkin Building - perhaps the most obvious as well as the most significant eco-friendly feature is the glass windows, which allow light to pass through the building, both reducing heating costs and brightening up the workspace. The ingenuity behind the various eco-friendly aspects of the Gherkin has seen its fair share of publicity both from serious and silly sources. In a recent April Fool’s Day edition, one e-publication printed a story detailing plans to replace 50% of the current exterior with grass, which would not only make large steps in the name of sustainability, but also give the building the green hue that would truly earn it the nickname of the Gherkin.

[03:29] AUDIO: The only drawback is as you may have guessed, that this story was an April Fool’s Day joke and completely made up. In all seriousness though, the building is setting a new standard of design that other architects and city planners just cannot ignore. The building’s bold and cost-efficient design has won a number of architectural awards, including the Stirling Prize, the London Region Award, and the Emporis Skyscraper Award among others. The design comfortably accommodates a large number of offices while keeping maintenance and operational costs down, striking a superb balance between nature and the workplace. Nature is well and good, as long as the weather is nice outside. Given London’s notoriously bad weather, the architects knew they must devise a quality temperature regulation system, and that they did.

[04:33] AUDIO: A special system designed to reduce the building’s reliance on air-conditioning was devised that cuts consumption in half compared to standard office buildings. There are atria that link each floor vertically to one another, forming spiraling spaces up the entire building. They serve not just as social common spaces but also act as the building’s lungs, distributing clean air from the opening panels in the facade through the entire building. The building isn’t all business though - it has its fair share of fun as well. At the very top, a clubroom offers a picturesque entertainment spot for company functions, private parties, etc., with a breathtaking panoramic view of the city. The creation of such an innovative structure has many wondering what the future of urban planning and architecture may be. Well, if the other projects currently commissioned by Foster and Partners are any indication, the entire city constructed with similarly eco-friendly buildings is not far in the distance.

[05:45] AUDIO: The Masdar City development aims to create a desert city that produces zero waste and removes as much carbon dioxide from the atmosphere as it puts in - a huge feat in protecting our earth. The Gherkin is a truly impressive feat, yet it is not the only one worth noting. Now to move on to another green initiative, I’ll tell you about the Eden Foundation Building, found in Cornwall…

explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "In 2003, construction was completed on the famous Swiss Re Building, or more informally called the Gherkin, a true masterpiece commissioned by the law offices of Foster and Partner. This is not the first ambitious endeavor of the film - they are renowned for their various philanthropic, environmental efforts."
explanation.step3: Loại từ cần điền: noun hoặc adjective Nghe tới tên tòa nhà the Gherkin => Biết đáp án sắp tới Nghe thấy " commissioned by the law offices of Foster and Partners" => Foster and Partners là law firm => Đáp án: law

questions.prompt: Its shape is like a _____.It can reduce the carbon _____ of the city.It lets _____ pass through the building, both reducing heating costs and brightening up the workspace.One false story claimed that the exterior of the building is partly made of _____.Architectural concept:

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The Gherkin, with its cutting edge green initiative and sharp design, is gaining recognition as an icon in modern architecture. You can pick it out of the London skyline by its unorthodox cigar shape."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe về hình dáng của tòa nhà => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe "...with its cutting edge green initiative and sharp design" (đề cập tới thiết kế tòa nhà) Nghe thấy "you can pick it out of the London skyline by its unorthodox cigar shape " => Có thể nhận diện tòa nhà này qua hình dáng giống điếu xì gà => Đáp án: cigar

questions.prompt: Links _____ with the workplace.Relies less on _____ for temperature control than other similar buildings.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "While its appearance is the obvious attribute at which to marvel, there is far more to this building than meets the eye. And let’s face it - there’s a lot about this building that meets the eye. The building helps reduce the city’s carbon footprint in a number of ways. Just a quick note - in case you’re not familiar with the term ‘carbon footprint’, get used to it! It’s a buzzword you’ll hear relentlessly to talk about reducing emissions. Think o"
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe xem tòa nhà có thể giảm carbon gì của city Nghe tới "There is far more to this building than meets the eye " => Có nhiều thứ thú vị về tòa nhà này hơn là chỉ về vẻ bề ngoài => Chuyển hướng nói từ vẻ bề ngoài qua chức năng của tòa nhà => Biết đáp án sắp tới Nghe thấy "the building helps reduce the city's carbon footprint in a number of ways" => Giúp giảm carbon footprint bằng vài cách => Đáp án: footprint

questions.prompt: The atria that let fresh air pass through the interior are known as _____.There is a place for entertainment called the_____at the top of the building.The future of urban planning and architecture:

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "So going back to the Gherkin Building - perhaps the most obvious as well as the most significant eco-friendly feature is the glass windows, which allow light to pass through the building, both reducing heating costs and brightening up the workspace."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe xem cái gì đi xuyên qua tòa nhà Nghe thấy nói tới " glass windows, which allow light to pass through the building" => Cửa kính cho phép ánh sáng đi xuyên qua tòa nhà => Đáp án: light

questions.prompt: It is likely that the entire _____ will be designed with more similarly eco-friendly buildings in future.A new building will be constructed aiming to produce zero waste and remove carbon dioxide from us as much as possible.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "In a recent April Fool’s Day edition, one e-publication printed a story detailing plans to replace 50% of the current exterior with grass, which would not only make large steps in the name of sustainability, but also give the building the green hue that would truly earn it the nickname of the Gherkin. The only drawback is as you may have guessed, that this story was an April Fool’s Day joke and completely made up."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe xem theo false story, thì bên ngoài căn nhà được làm bằng chất liệu gì Nghe tới April Fool's day => Ngày cá tháng tư, có liên quan tới a false story trong đề => Đáp án sắp tới Nghe thấy "a story detaling plans to replace 50% of the current exterior with grass " => Kế hoạch thay thế 50% phần mặt bên ngoài của tòa nhà bằng cỏ Sau đó nghe tiếp thấy " this story was an April Fool's day joke and completely made up " => Câu chuyện được bịa ra, không có thật => Đáp án: grass

questions.prompt: The atria that let fresh air pass through the interior are known as _____.There is a place for entertainment called the_____at the top of the building.The future of urban planning and architecture:

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "In all seriousness though, the building is setting a new standard of design that other architects and city planners just cannot ignore. The building’s bold and cost-efficient design has won a number of architectural awards, including the Stirling Prize, the London Region Award, and the Emporis Skyscraper Award among others. The design comfortably accommodates a large number of offices while keeping maintenance and operational costs down, striking"
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe về architectural concept của tòa nhà => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe "the building's bold and cost-efficient design has won a number of architectural awards" Nghe thấy "the design comfortably accommodates a large number of offices [...], striking a superb balance between nature and the workplace " => Thiết kế có sự cân bằng giữa thiên nhiên và nơi làm việc => Link thiên nhiên với nơi làm việc => Đáp án: nature

questions.prompt: It is likely that the entire _____ will be designed with more similarly eco-friendly buildings in future.A new building will be constructed aiming to produce zero waste and remove carbon dioxide from us as much as possible.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Nature is well and good, as long as the weather is nice outside. Given London’s notoriously bad weather, the architects knew they must devise a quality temperature regulation system, and that they did. A special system designed to reduce the building’s reliance on air-conditioning was devised that cuts consumption in half compared to standard office buildings."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe xem tòa nhà phụ thuộc vào cái gì ít hơn về mặt temperature control => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe "the architects knew they must devise a quality temperature regulation..." (= temperature control) Nghe thấy " reduce the building's reliance on air-conditioning " => Phụ thuộc ít hơn vào điều hòa (reduce reliance on = rely less on) => Đáp án: air-conditioning

questions.prompt: Complete blank for Question 38:

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "There are atria that link each floor vertically to one another, forming spiraling spaces up the entire building. They serve not just as social common spaces but also act as the building’s lungs, distributing clean air from the opening panels in the facade through the entire building."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe về phần atria của tòa nhà => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe "There are atria that link ...." Nghe thấy " they serve not just as social common spaces but also act as the building’s lungs , distributing clean air [...] through the entire building" => Không chỉ là nơi giao lưu xã giao mà còn có vai trò như là phổi của tòa nhà, phân phát không khí sạch cho cả tòa nhà => Atria còn được coi như những lá phổi => Đáp án: lungs

questions.prompt: Complete blank for Question 39:

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The building isn’t all business though - it has its fair share of fun as well. At the very top, a clubroom offers a picturesque entertainment spot for company functions, private parties, etc., with a breathtaking panoramic view of the city."
explanation.step3: Mình cần nghe về nơi dành cho việc giải trí trong tòa nhà => Biết đáp án sắp tới khi nghe " it has its fair share of fun as well" (fun có nghĩa liên quan tới entertainment) Nghe thấy "at the very top, a clubroom offers a picturesque entertainment spot" => Ngay tại đính của tòa nhà có clubroom, là địa điểm giải trí tuyệt đẹp => Đáp án: clubroom

questions.prompt: Complete blank for Question 40:

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The creation of such an innovative structure has many wondering what the future of urban planning and architecture may be. Well, if the other projects currently commissioned by Foster and Partners are any indication, the entire city constructed with similarly eco-friendly buildings is not far in the distance."
explanation.step3: Nghe tới "...what the future of urban planning and architecture may be " => Biết đáp án sắp tới Nghe thấy "the entire city constructed with similarly eco-friendly buildings is not far in the distance " => Việc xây dựng các tòa nhà thân thiện với môi trường trong toàn thành phố có thể không còn xa (not far in the distance = in future) => Đáp án: city

Example

transcript: [02:01] Janet: Hello?
[02:02] Agent: Yes, I’d like to speak with Janet Evans, please.
[02:05] Janet: Speaking
[02:06] Agent: Hi Ms. Evans, this is Jim Rodriguez calling from Farrelly Mutual about your recent homeowner’s insurance inquiry
[02:14] Janet: Yes, hi. Thanks for returning my call.
[02:17] Agent: My pleasure. I understand you are potentially interested in insurance for a bungalow located a bit out of town. Could you give me the address?
[02:26] Janet: Sure, it’s 49 Greenway Court. Greenway is one word.
[02:31] Agent: Thank you. Alright, and would you prefer to be contacted via email or phone?
[02:36] Janet: Either one is fine - maybe try emailing me first and as an alternative I can give you my phone number.
[02:42] Agent: Great - and what is your email address?
[02:45] Janet: pk2@cat.com.
[02:48] Agent: Hm, did you say “cat”, as in the animal?
[02:52] Janet: Yes. It is the acronym for the construction company I work for - I’m sure you’ve seen them around.
[02:57] Agent: Yes, I have. And could you give me your primary phone number, and the best time to reach you?
[03:03] Janet: Sure - the number is (020) 4251-9443. I am generally unable to answer my phone at work, but anytime after 5.30 p.m is fine.

[03:15] Agent: I will make a note of that here. Now I’m going to ask you a little bit about the property itself so we can make an accurate estimate of the cost of insuring your home. Could you tell me the size of your house?
[03:28] Janet: Um, well, I don’t have the exact measurements, but I’m pretty sure it’s right around 80 square metres. Should I measure it and call you back later?

[03:36] Agent: No, that’s completely alright. I’ll write 80 square metres for now to get the estimate and then an agent will come get the exact measurements later on if you decide to purchase our insurance.
[03:49] Janet: Okay, great.
[03:51] Agent: And what material is your house made of? For example, wood, brick, stucco,...
[03:56] Janet: It’s mainly brick.
[03:57] Agent: Great - that will give you a lower rate than most other materials since it is so strong.
[04:04] Janet: Wonderful!
[04:05] Agent: And do you have any sort of home security, Ms.Evans?
[04:08] Janet: Um, we don’t have a fence or anything yet, but we have an alarm system that we use regularly.
[04:14] Agent: Good. Now I’ll go through a number of things we offer coverage for, and I’d like you to tell me which items you want your policy to cover.
[04:57] Janet: Okay.
[04:57] Agent: We’ll start with the building itself first - would you like us to cover incidental damage to the structure to your house?
[05:05] Janet: Absolutely.

[05:06] Agent: Splendid. And the contents inside your house - we usually cover all items with an appraised value above £200. Would you like us to cover theft and damage beyond natural wear-and-tear? I will let you know that the second option here will come with a considerable increase in your rates.
[05:25] Janet: I think I’d just like the contents of the house to be covered against theft then.
[05:30] Agent: Alright - and would you like any other insurance - fire, flood, etc?
[05:35] Janet: Yes - definitely want flood coverage. It rains a lot here, and the drainage system in the area is not the greatest.
[05:42] Agent: Okay. I am calculating your quotation now. It will just take a second. (Two seconds pause) It looks like your annual insurance rate will be £148.30.
[05:54] Janet: Thanks, that seems somewhat reasonable. I would like to take some time to think about it. How long does it take to begin receiving coverage after signing up?
[06:04] Agent: It depends on the time of year - it can take anywhere from two to six weeks. I would say if you sign up by July 1st, you could start your coverage by August 1st.
[06:16] Janet: I see. Okay, thanks for your help. Should I call you back at this number when I have made my decision?
[06:22] Agent: Yes, please. And so that we can look up your account faster, I’ll give you a reference number that you should provide when calling. Ready?
[06:31] Janet: Yep!
[06:32] Agent: It’s TR278Q.
[06:35] Janet: Got it. Thanks!
[06:37] Agent: Thank you, and have a nice day!
